title: POC Intake — Workload Onboarding & Streaming Decisioning
next_steps: Jordan to share POC benchmark template and sample load scripts by 2026-08-27
Customer to provide representative traffic sample and 1k message trace by 2026-09-01
Schedule 1st run of streaming vs non-streaming test (target week of 2026-09-08)
Priya to propose KV cache warmup plan and suggested prefix caching settings
action_items: Jordan Lee: send benchmark template + onboarding checklist (due 2026-08-27)
Ellen Ruiz: export anonymized 24h traffic trace and sample prompts (due 2026-09-01)
Priya Nandakumar: draft streaming fallback strategy and warm-up sequence (due 2026-09-03)
Daniel Kim: confirm output quality examples / acceptance criteria (due 2026-09-03)
summary: Initial POC scoping for throughput/latency acceptance and harness integration. Main decision: whether to run customer workload in streaming mode (preferred for low-latency UX) versus batch/non-streaming for simpler harness compatibility and lower GPU utilization. Discussed success criteria (p95 tail latency, cost per 1M tokens, correctness thresholds), need for representative traces, prefix/KV cache warmup, and rollout timeline. Agreed next steps and deliverables.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining from Aurelia and appreciate the time. we'll keep this tight, 45 to 60 minutes, mostly scoping. I'm Jordan from Redwood - AE. priya is our systems SE who will pair on the benchmark design. can folks say quick hi and roles?
[00:00:18] Samir Patel: yeah hi this is samir, cto at aurelia. we're evaluating inference platforms for an assistant feature inside our trading desk app. main concerns are latency and deterministic tail behavior.
[00:00:26] Ellen Ruiz: ellen, platform eng. I'll own integrating the harness into our test infra.
[00:00:30] Daniel Kim: daniel, ml eng, I'll validate model outputs and score quality.
[00:00:34] Rachel Moore: rachel, product, here for success criteria and timelines.
[00:00:38] Priya Nandakumar: thanks all, priya here. quick agenda: align on acceptance criteria, walk through workload shape, decide streaming vs non-streaming for the POC, and define telemetry/action items.
[00:00:48] Jordan Lee: great, quick callouts: we usually run a 2–3 week POC: week 0 onramp and script handoff, week 1 baseline runs, week 2 tuning and live replay. timeline flexible — what are you expecting?
[00:01:02] Samir Patel: timeline a bit compressed — we'd like results within three weeks, but can do an initial baseline in one week if we prioritize the right metrics.
[00:01:10] Rachel Moore: business needs: p95 under 500ms for short queries (<=128 tokens) and p95 under 800ms for longer generative flows. also cost target: less than $X per 1M tokens — we'll fill exact later.
[00:01:22] Priya Nandakumar: ok noted. acceptance gates we propose: p95 latency, 99th in worst-case load, and a quality threshold measured on a labeled prompt set — daniel can speak to that.
[00:01:32] Daniel Kim: we'll supply ~200 labeled prompts for quality checks; pass/fail based on BLEU-ish style score and manual review—want to avoid hallucination on finance content.
[00:01:42] Jordan Lee: excellent. next, workload: ellen, can you describe your traffic shape — burstiness, concurrency, typical request size?
[00:01:50] Ellen Ruiz: typical is steady daytime traffic ~120 rps, bursts up to 800 rps for market events. average tokens per request around 60 tokens, but we have occasional 400-token long-form analysis. expected QPS for POC: we can emulate peak slice of 200–300 rps.
[00:02:05] Priya Nandakumar: that's helpful. For a realistic benchmark we recommend three slices: baseline steady (120 rps), peak slice (300 rps with tail spikes), and replay of historical burst windows. we'll need traces for exact timing.
[00:02:18] Samir Patel: we can provide a 24-hour anonymized trace with timestamps and token counts.
[00:02:22] Jordan Lee: perfect — that will let us synthesize arrival patterns for the harness. On streaming vs non-streaming: daniel, are your clients currently streaming?
[00:02:32] Daniel Kim: our frontend uses server-sent events for progressive responses in the assistant. product likes streaming for UX — partial tokens are shown as they arrive. but our current load test harness is non-streaming, so there's some work to do.
[00:02:45] Priya Nandakumar: that's the classic tradeoff — streaming preserves perceived latency but complicates batching and throughput on the GPU since tokens interleave. Non-streaming is simpler for harnesses and can increase throughput efficiency. For POC, we can run both: streaming to validate tail latency and UX, non-streaming to benchmark max throughput and cost-per-token.
[00:03:03] Rachel Moore: can you run both in the same POC without blowing the schedule?
[00:03:07] Priya Nandakumar: yes, if we accept a two-phase run: phase A non-streaming baseline runs (48 hours of mixed slices) then phase B streaming runs focused on tail and client behavior (24–48 hours). each phase has different harness configs.
[00:03:20] Ellen Ruiz: question: what does Redwood need to support streaming in the harness — do we need a client adapter?
[00:03:25] Jordan Lee: we have a streaming adapter for common clients (SSE/websockets) and will provide an example Node/python client. if you need custom auth or proxy behavior inside your VPC we'll work with you on the adapter.
[00:03:36] Samir Patel: security: we operate in a regulated environment — SOC2, quarterly audits. any PII needs to be scrubbed. can you run this inside a private deployment or VPC?
[00:03:45] Priya Nandakumar: for the POC we can run on hosted but isolated with private networking to your VPC (Redwood Private mode) or use dedicated capacity. for audit logs and KMS integration we can provision role-based access and export logs, yes. we'll share our compliance docs.
[00:03:58] Rachel Moore: and data retention? we need logs retained 90 days for incident investigations.
[00:04:03] Jordan Lee: retention is configurable; for POCs we generally set 90 days but we can confirm S3 export options and log redaction settings.
[00:04:09] Priya Nandakumar: back to technical: warm-up strategy — the KV cache/prefix caching matters a lot for p95 on repeated prompts. we recommend a staged warmup: 1) static prefix injection of top 500 unique prefixes, 2) replay of trace windows to populate KV, 3) controlled synthetic warmup for extreme tails.
[00:04:27] Daniel Kim: can we control warmup cost? warmups could double tokens.
[00:04:30] Priya Nandakumar: yes, we cap warmup budget and we instrument cost/time. typically a targeted warmup for the top 1–5% of prefixes gives most benefits without huge cost.
[00:04:40] Jordan Lee: instrumentation — we'll ask your team to enable these telemetry points: per-request tokens, upstream latency, model variant, cache-hit ration, and client streaming frames. we'll produce a dashboard and per-route breakouts.
[00:04:52] Ellen Ruiz: is there automatic fallback if streaming overloads the serving pool?
[00:04:56] Priya Nandakumar: yes, Redwood supports a fallback policy: streaming -> partial-response with final chunk delivered as non-streaming; or streaming -> different model variant or dedicated pool. we'll test fallback in the POC.
[00:05:07] Samir Patel: what about quantization and perf? we need to know how much lower precision affects financial correctness.
[00:05:12] Jordan Lee: we won't change model parameters for POC unless you want to test a quantized variant. Daniel, for QA we can run side-by-side with full fp16 and an int8-ish profile and compare outputs on your labeled set.
[00:05:23] Daniel Kim: yes let's do side-by-side; we'll flag any hallucinations or numeric degradation.
[00:05:28] Rachel Moore: acceptance criteria recap? p95 under target, failure rate under 0.1% at test slice, quality pass rate >= 95% on labeled prompts, cost target TBD.
[00:05:36] Priya Nandakumar: I'll write the acceptance matrix and include exact metrics for p50/p95/p99, throughput, error budget, and quality scoring.
[00:05:42] Jordan Lee: one more operational item — harness integration: we support two modes for your scripts: 1) traffic mirroring where we replay live traces into Redwood, and 2) synthetic harness scripts that call the API directly. Which do you prefer?
[00:05:53] Ellen Ruiz: traffic mirroring is most realistic but we need to ensure no PII and that replay times preserve burst patterns. we may start with synthetic scripts to iterate faster.
[00:06:01] Priya Nandakumar: recommended approach: synthetic for early tuning, then traffic-replay for final acceptance. we'll give you adapters for both.
[00:06:07] Jordan Lee: I'll attach the benchmark template that maps trace -> slice definitions and a sample synthetic script.
[00:06:12] Samir Patel: on monitoring, we need runbook hooks — e.g., if p95 breaches 1s we want an automatic alert and temporary throttle. can Redwood trigger webhook alarms?
[00:06:21] Priya Nandakumar: yes webhooks/alerting possible. we'll also recommend throttles and autoscale policies for the Dedicated pool.
[00:06:28] Daniel Kim: about metrics granularity — we need token-level cost and model variant breakdown in the dashboard.
[00:06:33] Jordan Lee: we provide token-level cost buckets and per-model telemetry; we'll share an example dashboard link.
[00:06:39] Rachel Moore: what's the deliverable schedule again?
[00:06:41] Jordan Lee: action items: jordan sends template by 8/27; ellen provides anonymized trace by 9/1; priya drafts warmup and fallback doc by 9/3; daniel confirms labeled prompts by 9/3. we'll schedule baseline run for week of 9/8.
[00:06:55] Ellen Ruiz: sounds good. small question — do we need to sign an NDA or security form first?
[00:07:00] Jordan Lee: for traces and PII-safe artifacts we have an onboarding security questionnaire; i'll attach it and we can get legal looped if needed.
[00:07:06] Samir Patel: ok thanks. last thing — can we get a rough estimate of cost for the two-week run?
[00:07:12] Jordan Lee: we'll provide a ballpark in the template, but rough math: non-streaming throughput runs usually show best cost-per-token; streaming can be ~15–30% higher due to smaller batch sizes. exact numbers after we run your trace.
[00:07:24] Rachel Moore: ok great. any open questions?
[00:07:28] Daniel Kim: none from me.
[00:07:29] Ellen Ruiz: none.
[00:07:31] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. recap in email and i'll post the template + links. we'll target baseline run week of 9/8.
[00:07:39] Priya Nandakumar: thanks all, I'll include warmup patterns and a suggested test matrix.
[00:07:43] Samir Patel: thank you.
[00:07:45] Rachel Moore: thanks, bye.
[00:07:48] [00:07:48] Meeting ended
